description: Deep universal probabilistic programming with Python and PyTorch

latest_release.body:
## What's Changed
* Fix pyro parameter nodes not showing up in graph of pyro deterministic nodes [bugfix] by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3378
* Support for deterministic dependent samples in PyroSample [enhancement] by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3376
* Equalize effect handler by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3375
* Update mappings to Sphnix documentation of other projects [bugfix] by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3383
* Fix models not rendering after application of the equalize effect handler by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3387
* Support PyTorch 2.4 in tests by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3389
* Update CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md by @Swarnim114 in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3391
* add copyright and license headers to various files by @andife in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3384
* Make Predictive work with the SplitReparam reparameterizer [bugfix] by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3388
* Support for transformed distributions, based on stacking or concatenation transforms, in SplitReparam by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3390
* Support observations that require broadcasting in SplitReparam by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3392
* Type annotate `pyro.util.py` by @ordabayevy in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3393
* Fix torch documentation link by @fehiepsi in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3396
* Use more numerically stable `log1p` in examples/scanvi/scanvi.py by @kit1980 in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3397
* Maintenance fixes by @ordabayevy in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3398
* Effect handler that conditions a model on sample sites having the same value by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3395
* Fix EqualizeMessenger type annotations by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3401
* Add batched calculation option to `energy_score_empirical` in order to reduce memory consumption by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3402
* Update example reference by @emmanuel-ferdman in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3403
* Fix `IndepMessenger.__iter__` type annotation by @ordabayevy in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3406
* fix autodetermination of plate device when running in a device contexf by @ilia-kats in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3405
* attempt to add sphinx_copybutton by @mjste in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3408
* Fixed norm const for SBVM by @OlaRonning in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3411
* Doc note and assert that sbvm conc <= 10k by @OlaRonning in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3412
* Reconciling expert opinions example by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3413
* Add a centered variance option to the ClippedAdam optimizer by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3415
* Update intro_long.ipynb by @yannickeich in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3420
* Use the new github template by @fehiepsi in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3421
* don't log to the root logger by @ilia-kats in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3422
* fix datapath bart data by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3425
* Use datasets from GitHub instead of CloudFront. by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3427
* Update CI to latest Ubuntu image. by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3428
* Update CI Python version to 3.12. by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3429
* Support changing the function used to calculate the euclidean distance in energy_score_empirical. by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3431
* Fix docker build by @BenZickel in https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/pull/3432
* Fixes #3430 (serializing an easyguide corrupts it). by @BenZickel in https://g

detail.readme: ----------------------------------------- [![Build Status](https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/actions) [![Coverage Status](https://coveralls.io/repos/github/pyro-ppl/pyro/badge.svg?branch=dev)](https://coveralls.io/github/pyro-ppl/pyro?branch=dev) [![Latest Version](https://badge.fury.io/py/pyro-ppl.svg)](https://pypi.python.org/pypi/pyro-ppl) [![Documentation Status](https://readthedocs.org/projects/pyro-ppl/badge/?version=dev)](http://pyro-ppl.readthedocs.io/en/stable/?badge=dev) [![CII Best Practices](https://bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org/projects/3056/badge)](https://bestpractices.coreinfrastructure.org/projects/3056) [Getting Started](http://pyro.ai/examples) | [Documentation](http://docs.pyro.ai/) | [Community](http://forum.pyro.ai/) | [Contributing](https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) Pyro is a flexible, scalable deep probabilistic programming library built on PyTorch. Notably, it was designed with these principles in mind: - **Universal**: Pyro is a universal PPL - it can represent any computable probability distribution. - **Scalable**: Pyro scales to large data sets with little overhead compared to hand-written code. - **Minimal**: Pyro is agile and maintainable. It is implemented with a small core of powerful, composable abstractions. - **Flexible**: Pyro aims for automation when you want it, control when you need it. This is accomplished through high-level abstractions to express generative and inference models, while allowing experts easy-access to customize inference. Pyro was originally developed at Uber AI and is now actively maintained by community contributors, including a dedicated team at the [Broad Institute](https://www.broadinstitute.org/). In 2019, Pyro [became](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press-release/2019/02/pyro-probabilistic-programming-language-becomes-newest-lf-deep-learning-project/) a project of the Linux Foundation, a neutral space for collaboration on open source software, open standards, open data, and open hardware. For more information about the high level motivation for Pyro, check out our [launch blog post](http://eng.uber.com/pyro). For additional blog posts, check out work on [experimental design](https://eng.uber.com/oed-pyro-release/) and [time-to-event modeling](https://eng.uber.com/modeling-censored-time-to-event-data-using-pyro/) in Pyro. ## Installing ### Installing a stable Pyro release **Install using pip:** ```sh pip install pyro-ppl ``` **Install from source:** ```sh git clone git@github.com:pyro-ppl/pyro.git cd pyro git checkout master # master is pinned to the latest release pip install . ``` **Install with extra packages:** To install the dependencies required to run the probabilistic models included in the `examples`/`tutorials` directories, please use the following command: ```sh pip install pyro-ppl[extras] ``` Make sure that the models come from the same release version of the [Pyro source code](https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro/releases) as you have installed. ### Installing Pyro dev branch For recent features you can install Pyro from source. **Install Pyro using pip:** ```sh pip install git+https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro.git ``` or, with the `extras` dependency to run the probabilistic models included in the `examples`/`tutorials` directories: ```sh pip install git+https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro.git#egg=project[extras] ``` **Install Pyro from source:** ```sh git clone https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro cd pyro pip install . # pip install .[extras] for running models in examples/tutorials ``` ## Running Pyro from a Docker Container Refer to the instructions [here](docker/README.md). ## Citation If you use Pyro, please consider citing: ``` @article{bingham2019pyro, author = {Eli Bingham and Jonathan P. Chen and Martin Jankowiak and Fritz Obermeyer and Neeraj Pradhan and Theofanis Karaletsos and Rohit Singh and Paul A. Szerlip and Paul Horsfall and Noah D. Goodman}, title = {Pyro: Deep Universal Probabilistic Programming}, journal = {J. Mach. Learn. Res.}, volume = {20}, pages = {28:1--28:6}, year = {2019}, url = {http://jmlr.org/papers/v20/18-403.html} } ```
